scope: Theorem 4.1 (Angular transfer estimate) of the manuscript “Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4” (preprints/Square-lattice-FK-interfaces-and-nested-loops-for-1-leq-q-lt-4-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d2ffa94ece599e88), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 23-24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a compact interval I ⊂ (−v, v). Let Bin be a product of Pζ rows and Bout a product of Pξ rows, at real angles in [−v, v]. Suppose each product contains at least n ≥ 1 angles in I. Uniformly for x, y ∈ [−v, v], ∥BoutN(x)Bin∥ ≤ Cn−1+ρ , (4.5) ∥Bout{N(x) − eiτ(x−y) N(y)}Bin∥ ≤ Cn−1−ρ . (4.6) The constant depends on q and I. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of N, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately 23 to its left. The two terms in (4.6) may use different such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts. Multiplication of D by a common scalar multiplies the bounds by its absolute value. The same estimates hold in the physical square array sliced in a diagonal time direction: its time angles are ±γ0, where γ0 = π/4, and its space angles alternate between π − γ0 and γ0. The exterior states may contain any finite number of physical row and spin insertions outside the sandwich. A scalar contraction is bounded by the displayed rate times the two reflection norms, with the squares centered on a cut included in its reflection kernel.
